[EFFECT]
The hour of the day is the most complex driver of bike demand, showing a clear double-peak pattern rather than a simple rise or fall. Demand is strongly suppressed in the early morning (roughly 1 AM to 5 AM, with the lowest point around 4 AM), then rises sharply through a morning rush-hour peak at 8 AM. After a moderate mid-day plateau (9 AM–3 PM), demand climbs again to its highest point of the day at 5 PM, before gradually declining through the evening and into the night.

[IMPORTANCE]
Hour of the day is by far the most important feature in the model — ranked 1st out of 9 features, with an importance score nearly double what you'd expect from a typical feature. It has a greater influence on predicted demand than temperature, weather, or any other variable.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Bike availability and staffing should be concentrated around the two daily peaks — approximately 7–9 AM and 4–6 PM — while overnight periods (especially 2–5 AM) can be used for maintenance and rebalancing with minimal disruption to riders.
